title: LockApp
tagline: B2B SaaS for Indian phone retailers to remotely manage Android devices sold on EMI
audience: Smartphone financing companies, NBFCs, and multi-store electronics retailers across India
role: Full-Stack Architecture, Android Device Owner Client & Cloud Backend
description: LockApp is an enterprise-grade mobile device management and EMI payment compliance platform built for electronics retailers, smartphone distributors, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The system couples an Android device administrator agent with a resilient cloud control plane to protect financed hardware assets.
challenge: Electronics retailers and financing firms face significant default risks when financing smartphones without collateral. Customers can remove SIM cards, turn off Wi-Fi, or attempt hardware resets to evade payment obligations, rendering standard cloud-based locks ineffective.
constraints: Zero network dependency for policy enforcement once deployed
Immunity against hardware factory reset via recovery menus
Low battery footprint with Android Device Admin background services
Carrier-agnostic SMS fallback when mobile data and Wi-Fi are disconnected
whatWeBuilt: Low-level Android Kotlin Device Owner agent with persistent watchdog service
Event-driven Node.js backend managing fleet policy states and IMEI registries
Secure multi-tenant retailer administration dashboard on Railway and MongoDB Atlas
Dual-channel lock/unlock signaling via Firebase Cloud Messaging and Fast2SMS triggers
approach: We adopted Android Enterprise Device Owner provisioning combined with an SMS data fallback mechanism to guarantee policy enforcement even when mobile data connectivity is intentionally cut.
solution: Vesharo engineered a dual-layer MDM architecture combining a low-level Android Kotlin Device Owner lock app with a distributed Node.js/Express backend on Railway with MongoDB Atlas. FCM lock/unlock signals are coupled with Fast2SMS fallback triggers, ensuring offline policy enforcement even when network connectivity is severed.
architecture: Kotlin Android Enterprise Device Owner client with persistent watchdog
Event-driven Node.js & Express backend managing fleet telemetry and policy states
MongoDB Atlas cluster with tenant-isolated retailer reporting and audit trails
Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) with automated Fast2SMS fallback triggers
deliverables: Production-ready Android Device Owner APK with automated provisioning flow
Cloud backend API service deployed on Railway with MongoDB Atlas cluster
Web-based retailer portal for device tracking and lock dispatch
Technical documentation and store provisioning standard operating procedure (SOP)
verifiedOutcomes: Multi-tenant retailer fleet management live in production
Tamper-resistant local lock enforcement active across enrolled devices
Operational dual-channel SMS + FCM lock dispatch verified across carriers
metrics: Real-time remote device policy sync across multi-tenant retailer accounts
Tamper-resistant offline lock enforcement preventing unauthorized bypass
Centralized retailer administration dashboard with automated EMI reconciliation

title: NavratriOS
tagline: Multi-tenant SaaS digitizing Navratri festival registration and gate entry in Gujarat
audience: Cultural festival organizers, large garba venue managers, and ticketing partners across Gujarat
role: High-Concurrency Backend, Offline QR Protocol & Handheld Scanner App
description: NavratriOS is a high-throughput ticketing and gate-entry management SaaS platform engineered to manage massive crowds at large cultural festivals and venues in Gujarat. Built for high peak concurrency, it delivers instant offline QR pass verification, instant anti-passback protection, and real-time crowd telemetry.
challenge: During large-scale multi-day cultural events, venue gates experience massive rushes of tens of thousands of attendees arriving within a narrow 90-minute window. Network connectivity at crowded physical gates is frequently congested, leading to scanner freezes, long entry queues, and ticketing fraud.
constraints: Congested cellular networks and intermittent gate Wi-Fi
Instant offline verification per attendee to avoid physical queue hazards
Strict anti-passback enforcement to eliminate screenshot and token sharing
Asynchronous batch-syncing to maintain entry velocity without connectivity loss
whatWeBuilt: Offline-first React Native gate scanner with sub-200ms cryptographic QR verification
Modular Node.js and Express event ticketing backend designed for peak concurrency
MongoDB database cluster with in-memory anti-passback verification checks
Web portals for event organizers, ticketing sponsors, and garba dance academies
approach: We designed an offline cryptographic verification model where passes are signed with asymmetric keys and validated locally on handheld devices, asynchronously syncing scans with central servers when connections restore.
solution: Vesharo architected a modular Node.js/Express backend backed by MongoDB and an offline-tolerant QR verification protocol. Handheld React Native/Expo gate scanners locally validate cryptographically signed QR tokens in under 200ms while asynchronously batch-syncing validation logs with the central server.
architecture: Modular Node.js/Express API architecture built for thousands of scans at peak
React Native & Expo handheld mobile scanner app with offline QR cryptography
MongoDB database cluster with in-memory anti-passback verification checks
Real-time administrative web portals for organizers and garba classes
deliverables: Cross-platform mobile scanner application compiled for Android handhelds
Ticketing administration web application with real-time gate telemetry
RESTful API services with containerized Docker deployment scripts
Staff operator runbook and offline synchronization protocol documentation
verifiedOutcomes: Pilot deployed at Gujarat festival venues during seasonal events
Sub-second gate validation demonstrated on handheld scanners under low-signal conditions
Event registration spikes handled during peak evening ticketing rushes
metrics: Sub-second gate validation via handheld scanners under dense crowd conditions
Zero-downtime registration spikes under heavy evening ticketing rushes
Real-time attendance analytics and pass management across multi-gate perimeters

title: Wirebench
tagline: Private API client with one-click Postman migration, drift detection & team changelog
audience: Backend engineering squads, API platform teams, and full-stack software architects
role: Core Architecture, Schema Diffing Engine & Desktop Client
description: Wirebench is a lightweight, privacy-first API testing and documentation workbench built for distributed engineering teams. It offers one-click migration from Postman, Insomnia, and Hoppscotch, continuously monitors live endpoint contracts against OpenAPI schemas, and flags breaking schema regressions.
challenge: As engineering teams scale microservices independently, subtle API contract drift—such as altered nullability, renamed response keys, or type shifts—routinely slips past unit tests, causing silent breakages across downstream web and mobile applications.
constraints: Zero transmission of proprietary API keys or endpoints to external cloud servers
Compatibility with complex nested OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 specification trees
Instant desktop performance with local-first file system persistence
Lossless conversion of nested Postman collection environments and scripts
whatWeBuilt: Local-first Electron and TypeScript desktop application with SQLite storage
AST-based schema comparison engine comparing live API payloads against OpenAPI specifications
Lossless one-click importer for Postman collections, Insomnia workspaces, and Hoppscotch
Automated visual diff viewer and markdown release changelog generator
approach: We built a privacy-first, local-first desktop application that runs diffing logic entirely on developer machines or in isolated CI pipelines without any outbound telemetry or proprietary data storage.
solution: Vesharo built Wirebench as an offline-capable, local-first API workbench that executes contract diffing directly on developer machines or within private VPC CI pipelines. It generates automated visual diffs and markdown changelogs with zero third-party cloud data exposure.
architecture: Local-first Electron & TypeScript desktop client with SQLite persistence
Automated schema comparison engine evaluating live JSON against OpenAPI 3.1 specs
One-click lossless importer for Postman collections, Insomnia, and Hoppscotch
Zero-telemetry privacy design ensuring proprietary API credentials never leave the machine
deliverables: Cross-platform desktop application installers for macOS and Linux
Embedded SQLite database migrations and local schema validation engine
Comprehensive OpenAPI 3.1 parser test suite with schema regression fixtures
Open source documentation and community contribution guidelines
verifiedOutcomes: Functional beta release undergoing internal engineering evaluation
Accurate detection of breaking schema regressions across complex JSON payloads
Zero external network requests made during test collection execution
metrics: Automated contract-drift alerting preventing breaking client regressions
Zero cloud data leaks — operates completely locally or in private VPCs
Integrated markdown changelog generation streamlining cross-squad releases
